- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.67) or volatile, model often underestimates or misses upward momentum; increase forecast slightly, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 5-10% for the next 3-5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2-5% for next 5-7 days unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in cycle (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is bullish; adjust downward by 1-3% for first 5 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-cycle, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 3-5% for next 3-5 days if sentiment drops below 0.33.
